clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient, immunosuppressed after kidney transplantation, presented with painful subcutaneous nodules accompanied by systemic symptoms including fever, cough, and weight loss. Dermatological examination confirmed subcutaneous nodules with erythematous and cyanotic skin. Skin lesion biopsy performed one year after symptom onset revealed proliferation of macrophages and intracellular microorganisms characteristic of Histoplasma capsulatum by methenamine silver stain, confirming fungal infection. Although fungal culture, chest imaging, and Histoplasma antigen or PCR tests were ordered, no documented results were available. The diagnosis and treatment of disseminated histoplasmosis were made one year after onset based on the biopsy findings and systemic clinical presentation.
